frequency_question: How often do executive agencies successfully strip recognized standard-setting monopolies of their official status when the political principals prioritize the action?
membership_rule: Includes any federal department review resulting in the formal withdrawal of national recognition from a major professional or institutional accreditor. Excludes routine renewals, voluntary relinquishments, or actions where the administration lacked an explicit stated intent to remove recognition.

cases.name: Department of Education review of the American Bar Association (prior threat/warning phases)
Department of Education termination of ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) recognition
Department of Education second termination of ACICS recognition after reinstatement attempts

coverage_note: 3 named major accreditation contestations involving high-stakes federal recognition status since 1980.
known_gaps: Minor specialized accreditors whose recognitions lapsed quietly or were resolved through administrative compliance rather than public revocation proceedings.
skeleton: Total administrative revocation attempts by the Department of Education against major national accrediting bodies where the political leadership pursued withdrawal of recognition.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major distinct contestations = 66 percent base rate for execution when intent is present.
validity_reason: Administrative law standards and Department of Education procedural frameworks for recognizing and derecognizing accreditors remain stable across multi-year presidential cycles.
